thread:
maya_support: Hey team — we've got an escalated ticket from a customer (Orion Health) saying their embedding calls suddenly started returning 1536-dim vectors instead of 768, which breaks downstream similarity code. They say nothing in their client changed.

maya_support: Pasted the minimal repro they sent. They hit /v1/embeddings with a project header and an org header. Example request they provided:

```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXXX' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: proj-orion' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: org-orion-health' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-lite","input":"patient note text..."}'
```

maya_support: Customer says their account was migrated between org keys last week (billing/legal), so they might be including both headers during rollout. They included a response example where the embedding array length is 1536.

maya_support: Ticket includes request-id: req_R123456789 and timestamp 2026-03-15T09:10:12Z (attached). Can someone check routing logs?

jordan_eng: Looking. I pulled the routing decision for req_R123456789 — the model selection log shows: route_reason=org_key_match, selected_model=text-embedding-3-large (1536) even though proj-orion is configured to use text-embedding-2-small (768).

jordan_eng: So the routing middleware currently prefers org-level mappings over project-level mappings. That matches the mismatch. If the customer is sending both X-Redwood-Org and X-Redwood-Project, the org mapping will win and override their project's pinned model.

priya_ml: That explains the dim mismatch. Many customers were pinned to 768-dim models; text-embedding-3-large is 1536. Embedding consumers downstream fail because vector size check fails.

ops_oncall: Is this a regression? We have a note in the routing config that org mappings were added to support vendor accounts. I need to know whether this precedence was intentional. It caused a production break for at least this customer.

jordan_eng: Checking Git history — last change was a month ago to add org-level overrides (RFC#2026-04). The intent was to let org admins set defaults. But we didn't account for explicit project headers in client requests during migration.

priya_ml: Quick mitigation options:
- Accept: revert org-priority change (hotfix) so X-Redwood-Project wins if present.
- Safer: detect dual headers and log + attach a warning to response (and roll out a short-term feature flag to prefer project when both present).
- Longer-term: require explicit model param in embeddings API so routing is explicit and unambiguous.

maya_support: Customer impact: high — their batch jobs failed and they turned off the feature. They asked for an immediate rollback or a targeted fix for their account.

jordan_eng: I can push a scoped rollback that changes precedence logic only for requests that contain both headers AND that are hitting /v1/embeddings. It's a small change in router.PriorityResolver. I'll open a PR and tag for emergency patch.

priya_ml: Also propose we add an automatic dimension-check response (non-breaking): when the server's selected model produces an embedding whose length != normative length for the customer's project config, return a 400-ish warning in response metadata and emit an alert. That would have given the customer an immediate signal.

maya_support: Can we get a reproducible test? I created a minimal test script (customer reproduced locally). Sharing here:

```python
import requests
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
headers = {
  'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-test-XXXXX',
  'X-Redwood-Project': 'proj-orion',
  'X-Redwood-Org': 'org-orion-health',
  'Content-Type': 'application/json'
}
payload = {'model': 'embed-lite','input':'hello'}
res = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(res.status_code, res.headers.get('X-Request-ID'))
print(res.json())
```

jordan_eng: Thanks. I ran it in staging; got the same behavior. Logged request path /router/resolver -> chosen_model: text-embedding-3-large.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for change set r/bugfix/routing-priority-17685 on infra-canary-2.

jordan_eng: PRed: https://github.com/redwoodinc/routing/pull/487 — changes PriorityResolver to treat explicit X-Redwood-Project header as highest precedence if present. Adds feature flag: routing.prefer_project_when_both_headers=true. Unit tests added.

ops_oncall: Deploying hotfix to prod-canary now. Will monitor 5 minutes for significance.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment succeeded on infra-canary-2 (instances: 4). Metrics: error-rate down, latency stable.

priya_ml: After patch deployed to canary, re-run the repro script (with both headers) — now selected_model=text-embedding-2-small and embedding length 768. Verified similarity pipeline in sandbox also OK.

maya_support: Customer notified about a potential fix. They requested immediate re-test from their side; asked for an option to pin their org to prefer project. I offered to coordinate while we roll the change to prod.

jordan_eng: Rolling to prod in stages. We'll enable feature flag true for the routing cohort and monitor model selection telemetry for next 24h. Also adding a one-off backfill: scan last 7 days for requests that had both headers and where selected_model dims != project pinned dims, then notify affected customers and offer remediation.

priya_ml: Follow-ups:
- Add explicit response header X-Redwood-Model-Dims and X-Redwood-Selected-Model for quick debugging.
- Emit a high-severity alert when dimension mismatch occurs for a customer with pinned dims.
- Add doc note in /docs/api/embeddings about header precedence and best practice: include only one of org or project whenever possible.

ops_oncall: I'll coordinate the backfill and alert rules. Please add runbook steps for support to triage if customer reports dim mismatch: include how to gather request-id, the two headers, and check /router/logs.

maya_support: Customer confirmed after our canary message that their test now returns 768 vectors in staging and asked for ETA for prod rollout. I told them 2-3 hours with gradual ramp and asked to keep us updated.

deploy-bot: Prod rollout started for r/bugfix/routing-priority-17685 — stage 1/4 (10% traffic).

jordan_eng: Post-rollout note: added a safety check to embeddings handler that returns a structured warning in metadata when vector length doesn't match project expectation. Example response snippet we added:

```json
{
  "data": [ { "embedding": [ ... ], "meta": { "model": "text-embedding-3-large", "dims": 1536, "warning": "dims_mismatch_project_expected_768" } } ]
}
```

maya_support: I'm updating the customer with the mitigation and next steps for docs and runbook. Closing loop once prod fully rolled and backfill completes.

ops_oncall: Backfill job queued; will report list of affected customers in ticket by EOD.

maya_support: Thanks all — great cross-team response.

jordan_eng: +1. Will follow up with PRs for telemetry and docs.

deploy-bot: Prod rollout completed (100% traffic) for r/bugfix/routing-priority-17685. No regressions detected.
